original_test_intent: Visually verify the Power Button LED is solid green after power-on and determine its behavior throughout BMC/HMC and POST initialization, while preserving undefined amber modes.
original_method: A qualified operator records the exact power-button indicator continuously from the approved power-on event through BMC/HMC initialization, POST completion and stable powered state, correlating video with console and power-state timestamps.
manual_activity: An on-site operator records continuous contextual and close video of the Power Button LED from power-on through named firmware phases, then confirms the final powered state without inferring undefined amber behavior.
required_inputs: Physical Power Button LED location and controller mapping
Authoritative decision whether the Green Blink section means blink or explicitly no blink
Expected color and cadence for each BMC, HMC, POST and steady-state interval
Observable phase markers and maximum initialization timing
Amber Solid/Blink definitions or revision-scoped N/A disposition
Power-state telemetry or register mapping, if available, with proof that it maps to the same LED
Approved power-on stimulus and independent recovery
safety_requirements: Do not power-cycle or reset outside the approved observation window
Do not treat a controller bit as proof of emitted color or cadence
Record the entire transition so a brief blink is not missed between sparse snapshots
Keep amber states unresolved instead of inventing fault stimuli
Stop on stalled POST, BMC/HMC unavailability, power instability or thermal/fault indication
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact source and physical/controller mapping inputs
Collect passive power, BMC/HMC, boot-stage and console timestamps
Prepare a phase-to-visual evidence matrix and correlate operator video
Read an approved LED/state register only as supporting evidence
Perform no power/reset action, physical observation, color/cadence judgment, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve Green Blink versus no-blink wording and define per-phase timing/cadence
Define or mark N/A the amber states by platform revision
Approve power stimulus and any register mapping
Review synchronized video and telemetry and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly refuses visual automation and asks about a register, but a register cannot replace optical evidence and the source polarity conflict remains.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use continuous operator video synchronized to BMC/HMC/POST phase evidence; any read-only controller state is corroboration only.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL VISUAL REVIEW PENDING GREEN-BLINK POLARITY DECISION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record one uninterrupted video across phase markers, extract timestamps for every visible transition and compare them to an approved phase/state matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact phase boundaries, cadence/timing, controller-to-physical mapping and recovery evidence without changing the ambiguous Master wording.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Telemetry cannot prove visible light output; amber modes remain unresolved, and no-blink cannot be accepted as Green Blink until engineering resolves the source.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sampling only the beginning and end can miss transient blinking during handoff between BMC/HMC and POST. The source places no-blink expectations beneath a Green Blink label, so either literal interpretation alone risks false acceptance.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve no-blink as the intended negative test or define an actual blink interval, but the decision must be revision-scoped and retain the original conflict history.
expected_evidence: Approved indicator mapping and phase/state decision matrix
Continuous contextual/close video from power-on through stable state
BMC/HMC/POST phase timestamps, console and passive power/controller evidence
Amber-state disposition and approved recovery confirmation
No-inferred-register/no-auto-retry audit, hashes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source creates a Green Blink section but instructs that the LED does not blink during BMC/HMC or POST, while Criteria still names Green Blink. Engineering must decide whether this is a negative blink test, a mislabeled section, or missing blink coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The power-on and initialization observation can be statically reviewed and manually captured. Final acceptance of the Green Blink state waits for the recorded engineering decision.

engineering_decision_pending: Resolve Functionality row 1912 Wistron-HW-00462-V002: whether Green Blink is an actual required state, an explicitly prohibited behavior throughout BMC/HMC and POST, or a mislabeled negative test; define phase boundaries, color/cadence/timing, amber-state disposition and any supporting register mapping while preserving Master.
review_improvement: Identifies the polarity conflict, requires uninterrupted phase-correlated evidence and prevents a state register or sparse snapshots from replacing physical acceptance.
independent_technical_reasoning: Boot LEDs can transition faster than an operator taking still photos, especially at controller ownership handoffs. A continuous recording tied to console phase markers is needed to prove absence of blink across both initialization domains. Because the section name and its instructions express opposite polarities, the reviewer cannot convert either interpretation into PASS without an authoritative state matrix.
